summary: Source decomposition of the zeta-function formalism and of the deduction of the Weil conjectures from the purity lemma, following Deligne, La conjecture de Weil I, Section 1 ((1.1)-(1.7) and (1.12)-(1.14)) read with proofs, the SGA 4 1/2 Rapport Section 3 (Theorems 3.1-3.2, Proposition 3.3, Corollary 3.4: L-functions from the trace formula) and Theorem 4.10 (statement), the SGA 4 1/2 Cycle Section 3 (Lefschetz trace formula in the proper smooth case via Kunneth and the trace morphism, Corollaries 3.7-3.8), and Weil II Corollary 3.3.9 (extension from projective to proper smooth). Stages WC.1, WC.2, WC.3 and WC.6 are partially decomposed; WC.0, WC.4, WC.5 (and its two sub-stages) and WC.7 are recorded as not read. The exact functional equation and the trace-formula proof itself (Rapport Sections 4-6) were not read. Independent review (REVIEW-EXT-03, 2026-09-16) re-read Weil I Section 1, the SGA 4 1/2 Rapport Section 3 with Theorem 4.10 and the Cycle Section 3, and corrected three nodes; see the review object.

nodes.title: The zeta function as an Euler product over closed points and its logarithmic derivative in terms of point counts
nodes.statement: For X_0 separated of finite type over F_q, with |X_0| its closed points, deg(x) = [k(x) : F_q] and q_x = q^{deg x}: Z(X_0, t) = Π_{x∈|X_0|} (1 − t^{deg x})^{-1} ∈ Z[[t]], converging for |t| small, with ζ_{X_0}(s) = Z(X_0, q^{-s}). Identifying |X| (closed points of X = X_0 ×_{F_q} F̄_q) with X_0(F̄_q), the Frobenius F acts as x ↦ x^q, the fixed points of F^n are X_0(F_{q^n}), |X_0| is the set of F-orbits with deg(x) the orbit size, and N_n := #X_0(F_{q^n}) = Σ_{deg(x) | n} deg(x). Consequently t d/dt log Z(X_0, t) = Σ_{n>0} N_n t^n. For an endomorphism F of a finite-dimensional vector space, t d/dt log det(1 − Ft)^{-1} = Σ_{n>0} Tr(F^n) t^n; more generally (Rapport 3.3) for a finitely generated projective module M over a commutative ring A and f ∈ End(M), T d/dT log det(1 − fT)^{-1} = Σ Tr(f^n) T^n.
hypotheses: X_0 separated of finite type over F_q (Deligne writes 'variete algebrique'); the Euler product converges for |t| small because there are finitely many closed points of each degree.

The trace identity is proved in Rapport Proposition 3.3 for a finitely generated projective module M over an arbitrary commutative ring A: first replace (M, f) by (M ⊕ M', f ⊕ 0) to reduce to M free, then use the principle of permanence of algebraic identities to reduce to A an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, then additivity in short exact sequences to reduce to rank 1.
proofSteps: (1.4)(a)-(d): F-fixed closed points of X are the F_q-points; F^n-fixed points are the F_{q^n}-points; closed points of X_0 are F-orbits of size deg(x); each x ∈ |X_0| with deg(x) | n contributes deg(x) points to X_0(F_{q^n}).
(1.5.2): logarithmic derivative of the Euler product gives Σ_x deg(x) t^{deg x}/(1 − t^{deg x}) = Σ_n N_n t^n.

(1.5.3): verify for dim V = 1 and use additivity of both sides in a short exact sequence. Rapport Proposition 3.3 gives the same identity for a finitely generated projective module over a commutative ring, by the reduction recorded in the hypotheses.
acceptance: X_0 = Spec F_q: Z = (1 − t)^{-1}; X_0 = P^1: Z = 1/((1 − t)(1 − qt)); N_n for a finite etale scheme with a nontrivial component permutation is computed from orbit sizes (the WC.7 test).
N_r = Σ_{m|r} m a_m with a_m the number of closed points of degree m, and the Mobius inversion for a_m.

sources.excerpt: d) De b) et c) resulte la formule (1.4.1) #X^{F^n} = #X_0(F_{q^n}) = Σ_{deg(x)|n} deg(x).
sources.match: The finite-extension point-count formula that WC.1 must prove ('N_r = Σ_{m|r} m a_m').

nodes.title: Grothendieck's cohomological expression Z(X_0, t) = Π det(1 − F* t | H^i_c(X, Q_ℓ))^{(−1)^{i+1}} and its L-function generalization
nodes.statement: Let ℓ ≠ p. Grothendieck's Lefschetz formula #X^{F^n} = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^{*n}, H^i_c(X, Q_ℓ)) (Weil I (1.5.1)) yields Z(X_0, t) = Π_i det(1 − F* t, H^i_c(X, Q_ℓ))^{(−1)^{i+1}}, an identity in Q_ℓ[[t]] between an element of Z[[t]] and the Taylor expansion of an element of Q_ℓ(t). More generally (Rapport 3.1-3.2; Weil I (1.14)), for a constructible Q_ℓ-sheaf F_0 on X_0, L(X_0, F_0, t) := Π_{x∈|X_0|} det(1 − F_x t^{deg x}, F_0)^{-1} equals Π_i det(1 − F* t, H^i_c(X, F))^{(−1)^{i+1}}, as a consequence of the trace formula Σ_{x∈X^{F^n}} Tr(F^{n*}, F_x) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^{*n}, H^i_c(X, F)) for all n; the deduction compares logarithmic derivatives term by term using Proposition 3.3.
hypotheses: X_0 separated of finite type over F_q; ℓ ≠ p; H^i_c are Grothendieck's ℓ-adic cohomology groups with proper support, finite-dimensional and zero for i > 2 dim X (Weil I (1.3), (1.10)); F* is defined via the finite morphism F and the canonical isomorphism F*F ≅ F (Weil I (1.11)-(1.12)).

The trace formula itself (Rapport 3.2, deduced from Theorem 4.10 for K_0 ∈ D^b_ctf(X_0, Λ) with Λ a noetherian torsion ring killed by an integer prime to p) is an imported theorem: Rapport Sections 4-6 were not read. The atlas assigns it to UPSTREAM:CohomologicalPointCounting:TraceFormula.

Convention: the two sources normalize differently (Weil I: variable t, degrees over F_q; Rapport: T = t^f with q = p^f). The node states the Weil I form. Any consumer must fix one convention before combining them.
proofSteps: Normalization: Weil I works over F_q with the variable t and the q-Frobenius, giving (1.14.3) Z(X_0, F_0, t) = Π det(1 − F* t, H^i_c)^{(−1)^{i+1}}. The Rapport works with q = p^f and sets T = t^f, stating Theorem 3.1 as L(X_0, F_0) = Π det(1 − F* t^f, H^i_c)^{(−1)^{i+1}}. In either normalization both sides are formal power series with constant term 1 over a field of characteristic 0, so it suffices to compare T d/dT log.
Left side: T d/dT log L = Σ_{n>0} T^n Σ_{x∈X^{F^n}} Tr(F^n, F_x) (grouping closed points of degree d | n).
Right side: by Proposition 3.3, T d/dT log Π det(1 − F* T, H^i_c)^{(−1)^{i+1}} = Σ_n T^n Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^{*n}, H^i_c); the trace formula identifies the coefficients.
acceptance: Weil I (1.5.4): for F = Q_ℓ one recovers Z(X_0, t); for X_0 = P^1 the formula gives 1/((1 − t)(1 − qt)) with H^0 = Q_ℓ, H^2 = Q_ℓ(−1).
The right-hand side lies in Q_ℓ(t); rationality over Q is a separate step (next node).

sources.excerpt: (1.5.4) Z(X_0, t) = Π det(1 − F* t, H^i_c(X, Q_ℓ))^{(−1)^{i+1}}. Le membre de droite est un element de Q_ℓ(t). La formule affirme que son developpement de Taylor en t = 0, a priori une serie formelle dans Q_ℓ[[t]] de terme constant un, est dans Z[[t]], et est egal au membre de gauche
sources.match: The precise meaning of the cohomological formula as an identity of formal power series.

sources.locator: [Rapport] Section 3, Theorems 3.1-3.2 and the deduction of 3.1 from 3.2, p. 85 (extraction lines 5596-5660)
sources.excerpt: Theoreme 3.2.- Pour tout entier n, Σ_{x∈X^{F^n}} Tr(F^{n*}, F_x) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^{*n}, H^i_c(X, F)). Rappelons brievement la methode classique pour deduire 3.1 de 3.2.
sources.match: The trace formula statement and the logarithmic-derivative deduction of the L-function formula.

nodes.title: Z(X_0, t) is a rational function over Q with coprime numerator and denominator in Z[t] of constant term 1
nodes.statement: Since Z(X_0, t) ∈ Z[[t]] and its image in Q_ℓ[[t]] is the Taylor expansion of a rational function, the Hankel determinants H_k = det((a_{i+j+k})_{0≤i,j≤N}) vanish for k > M for suitable N, M; vanishing holds in Q_ℓ iff it holds in Q, so Z(X_0, t) ∈ Z[[t]] ∩ Q(t). Writing Z = P/Q with P, Q ∈ Z[t] coprime and positive constant terms, Fatou's lemma (Z ∈ Z[[t]] with constant term 1) forces the constant terms of P and Q to be 1.
hypotheses: Only the integrality of the coefficients (from the Euler product) and the cohomological rationality over Q_ℓ are used; no purity input.
Fatou's lemma is cited without proof; the Hankel criterion for rationality of power series is classical (not proved in the source).
proofSteps: Hankel criterion in both directions over Q_ℓ and over Q; the determinants are integers, so their vanishing is field-independent.

Fatou: a power series with integer coefficients that is rational has a representation with denominator of constant term 1; combined with the positive-constant-term normalization, both constant terms are 1.
acceptance: For X_0 a smooth projective curve of genus g, Q = (1 − t)(1 − qt) and P ∈ Z[t] of degree 2g with P(0) = 1 (once the P_i are identified, WC.3).
Uniqueness of the coprime representation with positive constant terms.

sources.locator: Section 1, proof of (1.7) => (1.6), first paragraph, p. 276 (extraction lines 197-215)
sources.excerpt: Cette nullite est vraie dans Q_ℓ si et seulement si elle l'est dans Q; Z(X_0, t) est donc le developpement en serie de Taylor d'un element de Q(t). En d'autres termes, Z(X_0, t) ∈ Z[[t]] ∩ Q(t) ⊂ Q(t). ... D'apres un lemme de Fatou, que Z(X_0, t) soit dans Z[[t]] et de terme constant un implique que les termes constants de P et Q sont 1.
sources.match: The rational-descent and normalization lemmas the stage lists ('Fatou/Gauss and rational-descent lemmas').

nodes.title: Lefschetz trace formula for endomorphisms of proper smooth varieties via Kunneth, the trace morphism and cycle classes
nodes.statement: Let X, Y be proper smooth varieties over an algebraically closed field k, purely of dimensions N and M, ℓ invertible in k. Via Kunneth H*(X × Y) = H*(X) ⊗ H*(Y), a class η ∈ H^{2q}(X × Y)(q) defines η_{XY}: H*(Y)(N − q) → H*(X), ξ ↦ ∫_Y η · pr_2^* ξ. (3.3) For p + q = N + M, ε ∈ H^{2p}(X × Y)(p), η ∈ H^{2q}(X × Y)(q): Tr_{X×Y}(η · ε) = Tr(η_{XY} ε_{YX}, H*(X)), the trace on the right taken in the graded (super) sense. (3.6) For q = M and η = cl(B) the class of a subscheme B ⊂ X × Y finite over X, η_{XY} = Tr_{B/X} ∘ pr_2^*; for B the graph of f: X → Y, η_{XY} = f^*. (3.7) For f an endomorphism of proper smooth X with isolated fixed points, Σ (−1)^i Tr(f^*, H^i(X)) is the number of fixed points counted with multiplicity (intersection multiplicity of the graph with the diagonal). (3.8) For X a curve over k obtained by base change from X_0/F_q and f the Frobenius, Σ (−1)^i Tr(f^*, H^i_c(X)) is the number of fixed points of f.
hypotheses: X, Y proper and smooth over an algebraically closed field; the trace morphism Tr: H^{2M}(Y)(M) → Q_ℓ and Poincare duality (isomorphism H*(Y) ≅ H*(Y)^∨) as in [Cycle] Section 1 and [Dualite]; cycle classes of [Cycle] Section 2 with the intersection-multiplicity interpretation (Remark 3.5, via an alternating sum of Tor).

Remark 3.4: the proof of Proposition 3.3 does not use that the duality maps θ_X, θ_Y are isomorphisms, nor smoothness of X and Y; but outside the smooth case there are few cohomology classes to apply it to. (The printed remark says "la preuve de 3.4", a misprint for 3.3.)
Corollary 3.8 handles non-smooth curves by reduction to the smooth locus and its projective completion (proof only partially read).
proofSteps: Fix an isomorphism Q_ℓ(1) ≅ Q_ℓ and retain only the Z/2-grading; η_{XY} is the image of η under H*(X) ⊗ H*(Y) ≅ H*(X) ⊗ H*(Y)^∨ = Hom(H*(Y), H*(X)); the definition of the trace then reduces 3.3 to Tr_{X×Y} = Tr_X ⊗ Tr_Y. The reduction uses 3.1: under Künneth the trace morphism H*(X × Y)(M) → H*(X) is H*(X) ⊗ (trace of H*(Y)(M) → Q_ℓ), and is homogeneous of even degree, so no sign problem arises.
3.6: by 3.2 and the projection formula for cl(B), η_{XY}(ξ) = Tr_{X×Y/X}(cl(B) · pr_2^* ξ) = Tr_{B/X}(pr_2^* ξ).
3.7: take A = graph of the identity, B = graph of f in 3.5 and apply 3.3 and 3.6.
acceptance: For X = P^1 and f = Frobenius, Tr(f^*, H^0) + Tr(f^*, H^2) = 1 + q = #P^1(F_q).
The statement is about ordinary cohomology of proper X; for open X the Rapport's compact-support trace formula is needed, which is not proved by this route.

sources.locator: [Cycle] Section 3, 3.1-3.3 with proof, Remarks 3.4-3.5, Proposition 3.6 with proof, Corollaries 3.7-3.8, pp. 150-152 (extraction lines 11672-11810)
sources.excerpt: Corollaire 3.7 - Soit f un endomorphisme de X propre et lisse sur un corps algebriquement clos k. On suppose que les points fixes de f sont isoles. Alors, la trace Σ(−1)^i Tr(f^*, H^i(X)) est le nombre de points fixes de f, chacun compte avec sa multiplicite.
sources.match: The duality-based Lefschetz formula, the only part of WC.2's duality package read; the functional equation is not derived here.

nodes.title: From the purity lemma to integral, ℓ-independent characteristic polynomials: Deligne's (1.7) => (1.6)
nodes.statement: Let X_0 be projective smooth over F_q and assume (1.7): for each i and ℓ ≠ p the eigenvalues of F* on H^i(X, Q_ℓ) are algebraic numbers all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q^{i/2}. Then (1.6): det(t·1 − F*, H^i(X, Q_ℓ)) has integer coefficients independent of ℓ, and its complex roots have absolute value q^{i/2}. Proof: with P_i(t) = det(1 − F* t, H^i(X, Q_ℓ)), (1.7) makes the P_i pairwise coprime, so Z = Π P_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} is in lowest terms and P = Π_{i odd} P_i, Q = Π_{i even} P_i. Let K ⊂ Q̄_ℓ be generated over Q by the roots of R = PQ; the roots of P_i are those roots of R all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q^{−i/2}, a set stable under Gal(K/Q), so P_i ∈ Q[t]; by Gauss's lemma (or because its roots are inverses of algebraic integers) P_i ∈ Z[t]; and this description of the roots is independent of ℓ, hence so is P_i.
hypotheses: X_0 projective and smooth ('non singuliere') over F_q; (1.7) is used for all i and all ℓ ≠ p, with the all-complex-conjugates formulation (not a single embedding).
Uses the rationality and normalization lemma (previous WC.1 node) and the cohomological formula; multiplicities are handled through the polynomial identity, not merely root sets.
Invertibility of F* (so that deg P_i = b_i) is not stated in this passage; it follows from the nonvanishing of eigenvalues asserted by (1.7).
proofSteps: Distinct absolute values q^{−i/2} of the roots of P_i for different i prevent common roots, so the alternating product is reduced.
Galois stability of the root set of P_i (characterized by the absolute values of all conjugates) gives P_i ∈ Q[t]; integrality by Gauss's lemma given P, Q ∈ Z[t] with constant term 1.
ℓ-independence: the characterization of the roots of P_i inside the ℓ-independent rational function Z(X_0, t) does not involve ℓ.
acceptance: For a smooth projective curve, P_1 ∈ Z[t] of degree 2g with reciprocal roots of absolute value q^{1/2}, independent of ℓ.
The argument does not assert semisimplicity of F*, nor does it use it.

sources.locator: Section 1, Theorem (1.6), Lemma (1.7) and the proof of (1.7) => (1.6), pp. 276-277 (extraction lines 189-230)
sources.excerpt: Les racines de P_i(t) sont celles des racines de R(t) ayant la propriete que tous leurs conjugues complexes sont de valeur absolue q^{−i/2}. Cet ensemble est stable sous Gal(K/Q). Le polynome P_i(t) est donc a coefficients rationnels.
sources.match: The all-conjugates Galois-stability argument the stage requires, with the ℓ-independence conclusion.

nodes.title: Extension of the Weil conjectures from projective to proper smooth varieties (Weil II 3.3.9)
nodes.statement: Let X_0 be proper and smooth over F_q. Then H^i(X, Q_ℓ) is pure of weight i, and for each i the polynomial det(t·1 − F, H^i(X, Q_ℓ)) has integer coefficients independent of ℓ (ℓ ≠ p) whose complex roots have absolute value q^{i/2}. Proof: the upper bound H^i_c mixed of weight ≤ i (3.3.4 with F = Q_ℓ, weight 0) and the lower bound H^i mixed of weight ≥ i for smooth X_0 (3.3.5, by Poincare duality) coincide for proper X_0, so H^i is pure of weight i; then argue as in Weil I (1.7) => (1.6). (3.3.7-3.3.8) For the constant sheaf, the pairs (r, s) = (v(α), v(qα^{-1})) of normalized p-adic valuations of Frobenius eigenvalues on H^i lie in the indicated triangles of the Hodge-type diagram (lower triangle in compact-support or proper cohomology, upper triangle in ordinary cohomology of smooth X). (3.3.11) 'Smooth' enters only through Poincare duality and may be replaced by the rational-homology-manifold condition Ra^! Q_ℓ = Q_ℓ(n)[2n], e.g. for etale-local quotients of smooth schemes by finite groups.
hypotheses: Weil II Theorem 3.3.1 (Rf_! preserves 'mixed of weight ≤ n + i') and its corollaries 3.3.4-3.3.6 are the inputs; they are recorded in the WeightsInEtaleCohomology packet and assigned by the atlas to DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.7, which explicitly exports 'the smooth proper nonprojective extension used by WC (3.3.9)'.
The integrality of the P_i still uses the Weil I argument (Fatou, Gauss) on the proper X_0; the trace formula holds for proper X_0 as well.
proofSteps: H^i_c(X, Q_ℓ) = H^i(X, Q_ℓ) for proper X; weights ≤ i from 3.3.4 and ≥ i from 3.3.5.
Purity of each H^i gives coprimality of the P_i and the rest of Weil I's argument applies verbatim.
acceptance: A proper smooth nonprojective variety (e.g. a Hironaka-type example) satisfies the same integrality and absolute-value statements as projective ones.
For G_m (smooth, not proper) the weights of H^1_c and H^1 differ (0 vs 2), illustrating why properness is needed for purity of the whole H^i.

sources.excerpt: Prenons X_0 propre et lisse. On trouve que H^i(X, Q_ℓ) est pur de poids i. Raisonnant comme dans I (preuve de (1.7) => (1.6)), on retrouve le theoreme principal (1.6) de I, avec « projectif » remplace par « propre »
sources.match: The exact mechanism of the projective-to-proper extension WC.6 asks for.

links.reason: The logarithmic derivative Σ N_n t^n and the identity T d/dT log det(1 − fT)^{-1} = Σ Tr(f^n) T^n are what the trace formula is compared with, term by term.
Rationality over Q_ℓ of Z(X_0, t) comes from the cohomological formula; the Hankel argument then descends it to Q.
The reduced representation Z = P/Q with P, Q ∈ Z[t] of constant term 1 is the starting point of the identification of the P_i.
Z = Π P_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} with P_i = det(1 − F* t, H^i) is the identity whose reducedness (from purity) identifies P = Π_{i odd} P_i and Q = Π_{i even} P_i.
The atlas assigns the proof of Lemma (1.7) (Weil I Sections 3-7: fundamental estimate, pencils, tensor-power argument) to DWP.2-DWP.4; WC.3 consumes the purity lemma in its all-conjugates form.

sources.locator: Section 1, Lemma (1.7) and 'La suite de cet article est consacree a la demonstration de (1.7)', p. 277

links.reason: EDC.2 owns the trace morphism Tr_f and Poincare duality for smooth proper varieties, which [Cycle] 3.1-3.3 use through Kunneth and the identification H*(Y) ≅ H*(Y)^∨ to define η_{XY} and to reduce 3.3 to Tr_{X×Y} = Tr_X ⊗ Tr_Y.

DWP.7's description states that it exports 'for constant coefficients the smooth proper nonprojective extension used by WC (3.3.9)' together with the Rf_! bound (3.3.1), the compact-support bound (3.3.4) and the duality lower bound (3.3.5) on which 3.3.9 rests.

checked.note: Weil I (1.1.1)-(1.1.3), (1.4) a)-d) with (1.4.1), (1.5.2) and (1.5.3) match at the cited lines, as does Rapport Proposition 3.3. Correction: the hypothesis described the trace identity as proved "in Sch12-style generality", which is meaningless here; it is proved for a finitely generated projective module over a commutative ring, and the proof first reduces to a free module. The proof steps now record that reduction.

Weil I (1.5.1), (1.5.4) and (1.12.1), (1.14.1)-(1.14.3) match, as do Rapport Theorems 3.1-3.2 and the term-by-term comparison of logarithmic derivatives, and Theorem 4.10 with its hypotheses on Λ. Correction: the first proof step read "Set T = t^f-free normalization as in the Rapport (T = t)", which is garbled. The Rapport sets T = t^f with q = p^f and states 3.1 with det(1 − F* t^f, H^i_c), while Weil I (1.14.3) uses t over F_q; both normalizations are now stated, with a hypothesis warning consumers to fix one.

The proof of (1.7) => (1.6), first paragraph, matches: the Hankel determinants vanish over Q_ℓ iff over Q, so Z ∈ Z[[t]] ∩ Q(t); P, Q coprime in Z[t] with positive constant terms; Fatou's lemma forces both constant terms to be 1. The packet correctly records that Fatou and the Hankel criterion are cited without proof.

[Cycle] 3.1, 3.2, Proposition 3.3 with its proof, Remarks 3.4-3.5, Proposition 3.6 with proof and Corollaries 3.7-3.8 match, including the Z/2-grading and Q_ℓ(1) ≅ Q_ℓ normalization, the identification η_XY ∈ Hom(H*(Y), H*(X)), the reduction to Tr_{X×Y} = Tr_X ⊗ Tr_Y, and the graph-of-f specialization. Additions: the even-degree argument of 3.1, and the printed misprint "la preuve de 3.4" for 3.3.

Theorem (1.6), Lemma (1.7) and the proof of (1.7) => (1.6) match in every step: coprimality of the P_i from distinct absolute values, P = Π_{i odd} P_i and Q = Π_{i even} P_i, the field K generated by the roots of R = PQ, Galois stability of the root set of P_i, Gauss's lemma (or inverses of algebraic integers) for integrality, and the ℓ-independence of the characterization. The packet's note that invertibility of F* is not stated in this passage is correct.

Weil II (3.3.7)-(3.3.11) and the derivation of Corollary (3.3.9) match: purity of H^i for proper smooth X_0 comes from the coincidence of the 3.3.4 upper bound and the 3.3.5 lower bound, and the rest is "raisonnant comme dans I (preuve de (1.7) => (1.6))". The (r, s) localization and the rational-homology-manifold variant are stated as in the source.
